title: Prime sequences with AP-gaps (generalization of Erdős #455)

problemStatement.formal: \text{Define } \mathrm{APGapPrimeSeq}(d) := \{q : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} : q \text{ strictly increasing prime sequence}, \forall n, q_{n+2} - 2 q_{n+1} + q_n = d\}. \text{ Determine: (i) for } d = 0, \text{ when does } \mathrm{APGapPrimeSeq}(0) \text{ contain length-} k \text{ prefixes (Green-Tao); (ii) for } d > 0, \text{ growth bound on } q_n.
problemStatement.plain: The parent erdos-455 studies prime sequences with monotonically non-decreasing gaps (g_{n+1} ≥ g_n). This sub-OQ generalizes: what if the gaps themselves form an arithmetic progression (g_{n+1} - g_n = d constant)? Two subcases: (1) d = 0 means primes in arithmetic progression — this is Green-Tao 2008 territory; (2) d > 0 means strictly increasing gap differences, a refinement of the parent's monotone-gap condition. The d > 0 case is, to the author's knowledge, a new mathematical question; the conjectured growth bound q_n = Ω(n^3) follows from a heuristic combining linear gap growth with prime-density constraints.
whyMatters: Direct extension of parent's monotone-gap framework with a tighter structural condition (second-order arithmetic).
The constant-gap subcase reduces to Green-Tao 2008 — a major modern theorem absent from Mathlib v4.26.0. Axiomatic formalisation here would be the gallery's first treatment of Green-Tao.
The d > 0 case poses a genuinely new question: are there arbitrarily long AP-gap prime sequences with strict d > 0? Manual enumeration suggests sparsity beyond length 4.

proven: Parent (verified, axiomatised): Erdős #455 monotone-gap framework with Richter 1976 axiom liminf q_n / n^2 > 0.352.
Dirichlet 1837: infinitude of primes in any AP {a, a+d, a+2d, ...} with gcd(a, d) coprime.
van der Corput 1939: infinitely many 3-APs in primes.
Green & Tao 2008: arbitrarily long APs in primes — a deep modern theorem.
Folklore: no infinite AP in primes (q_0 + q_0 · d is divisible by q_0 in {q_0, q_0+d, q_0+2d, ...}).
Heath-Brown 1981: three primes and almost-prime in AP — quantitative refinement.
AP-gap prime sequences with d > 0 are sparse in length-4 manual enumeration.
open: For d > 0: do arbitrarily long AP-gap prime sequences exist? Manual search suggests sparsity beyond length 4 for d = 2.
Exact growth bound: is q_n = Ω(n^3) the right order for d > 0 AP-gap sequences? Author's conjecture.
Computer-searchable: enumerate AP-gap prime sequences in first 10^5 primes for d ∈ {2, 4, 6, ...} and length k = 4, 5, ...
knownResults.goal: Formalize in Lean: (1) HasAPGaps and APGapPrimeSeq d structures. (2) Equivalence apGap_zero_iff_prime_AP. (3) Monotone-gap subsumption apGap_subsumes_monotone for d ≥ 0. (4) Axiom Green-Tao for prefix-AP statements (d = 0 subcase). (5) Conjectural cubic growth axiom for d > 0. (6) Optional concrete small-case witnesses via native_decide. Gallery entry status: axiomatized (Green-Tao non-negotiable).

insights: (S3 ACT BUILD-VERIFY) Mathlib v4.26.0 strict-parser trap for orphan `/-- ... -/` docstrings is real and silent on origin/main: parent Proofs/Erdos455Problem.lean had 3 orphan docstrings (after a prior commit removed an axiom but left its docstring intact) that broke compilation as soon as Docker built the file. Fix is the 2-char swap `/--` → `/-!` to reclassify them as section comments. Pre-build grep: `grep -nE '^/--$' proofs/Proofs/<parent-file>.lean` and inspect whether the NEXT non-comment token is a declaration. (See feedback_researcher_mathlib_v426_standalone_docstring_parser_strict.md.)
Sub-OQ splits into two structurally distinct subcases: d = 0 (Green-Tao territory, axiomatised) and d > 0 (genuinely new question on sparse strictly-AP-gap prime sequences).
For d > 0: a priori q_n = q_0 + n g_0 + binom(n, 2) d = Θ(n^2); tightening to n^3 requires combining with Vinogradov/Heath-Brown prime density constraints — research-grade.
Manual enumeration in S1 failed to find length-5 AP-gap prime sequences with d = 2 (tried q_0 ∈ {3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23} with various g_0): suggests strong sparsity.
Green-Tao 2008 is the only existing rigorous statement covering this OQ — and it's absent from Mathlib v4.26.0. Cannot be proven in a single iteration; must be axiomatised.

Cubic growth claim (S1) for d > 0 is heuristically false. For irreducible quadratic f(n), prime density is ~1/log n (Bunyakovsky-conjectural — not in Mathlib), giving logarithmic-not-cubic growth. S4 should drop cubic-growth axiom and replace with Bunyakovsky-style unbounded-length axiom.

Bridge pattern (S3 ACT): finitary form F1 of an axiomatized prime-existence theorem combines cleanly with predicate-style HasAPGaps q d via obtain + push_cast + ring. The same pattern will work for S4 (Bunyakovsky → APGapPrimeSeq d existence at arbitrary length).

Decidability provides axiom-free verification of small witnesses (S3 ACT k=5 case): the concrete length-5 instance of 5, 11, 17, 23, 29 follows from kernel reduction via decide; no Green-Tao axiom needed. This separates the existence-at-arbitrary-length claim (axiomatized) from concrete small-length certifications (verified).
